title: How he was invited to Argentina
summary: Two Argentine fans hear him in Copenhagen, listen to tapes at his house and arrange contracts; a Buenos Aires band sounds like Condon's.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And, then, you know last year I got a very big surprise I went down to Buenos Aires and how that all came about - in Buenos Aires, I was playing at the youth center in Copenhagen and two guys came; we didn't talk about this before - did we?
Two guys came to see me and they were from Buenos Aires and one was with the SAS ---

Airlines and he had a friend with him called Tito and they claimed that they came-- that they had been listening to my records in Buenos Aires for a year and they wanted to come and hear me personally - they heard I was there; one guy was 2,000 miles from there; he flew in just to get there for that night and the other guy was already in Copenhagen and, uh, they were so enthusiastic that when I got through playing that night, I said - why don't you come up to my house and I'll play some tapes and things. And, I suppose they were flabbergasted - is the word---

That I invited them up - so I invited them up to my house and we had some drinks and played some tapes and they said, how would you like to come to Argentina and as soon as they got back, I got a wire through the SAS saying that they were sending two people all the way from Argentina - that were going to Denmark anyway - to come with the contracts for me and this is how I got to Argentina. And, of course, Argentina, it was a love for me because I had no idea whether I was going to have to play rumba's and tangos and what the hell and I got down there and ran into the same damn thing-- there was a band that played almost identical to the old Condon band and I recorded with them and did a whole tour
- played all the concert halls - all the biggest concert halls and a big successful thing for me.
